roles.title: Senior Product Engineer
roles.oneLiner: Own features end to end in the codebase 400 boatyards use to run haul-outs, invoices, and winter storage.
whatYoudDo: Ship one meaningful thing most weeks — a clearer schedule view, a billing fix, faster search — and watch real yards use it within days.
Work the whole stack: Rails, Postgres, and a React front end, plus the occasional gnarly CSV import from a twenty-year-old yard system.
Talk to customers directly. A few times a month you'll get on a call with a yard manager and see your feature running in their shed office.
Review teammates' work kindly and get the same back — two engineers look at everything before it ships.
Take a real on-call rotation: roughly one week in six, almost always quiet, paid extra when it isn't.
Spend your first month shipping small fixes with a buddy, not sitting through onboarding decks.
whatYouWont: No sprint theater. We plan in six-week cycles with slack built in, and nobody rearranges your tickets overnight.
You won't wait on a platform team. There are nine engineers; if the deploy pipeline annoys you, you're allowed to fix it.
No growth-hack work. We don't build dark patterns, and marketing can't file engineering tickets.

howWeHire.title: Intro call — 30 minutes
howWeHire.detail: With our head of engineering. What you've built, what you want next, and an honest picture of the codebase, warts included.

howWeHire.title: Technical conversation — 60 minutes
howWeHire.detail: Walk us through something real you shipped. No live-coding gotchas, no whiteboard algorithms.

howWeHire.title: Paid work sample — half a day, $400
howWeHire.detail: A small task from our actual backlog, done on your own schedule, followed by a call about the choices you made.

howWeHire.title: Offer within a week
howWeHire.detail: We check two references, put numbers in writing, and give you a full week to decide. No exploding offers.

roles.title: Product Designer
roles.oneLiner: Design calm, unfancy screens for people who run a boatyard from a shed office with mud on the keyboard.
whatYoudDo: Design real workflows — invoicing, slip assignments, work orders — then pair with engineers until the shipped thing matches the design.
Visit customers. A few times a year you'll stand in a yard office in Maine or Maryland watching someone use your screens.
Own the design system with our other designer: one component library, boring on purpose, documented as you go.
Write the words. Labels, empty states, and error messages are part of the design here, not someone else's job.
Run usability calls with real yard managers, not proxies — we book them, you lead them.
whatYouWont: No portfolio-driven redesigns. The product looks plain because our users are busy; your job is clarity, not spectacle.
You won't fight for a seat at the table. Design has been in the room since the founding team.

howWeHire.title: Intro call — 30 minutes
howWeHire.detail: With our design lead. Where you've worked, how you like to work, and what we're honestly like to design for.

howWeHire.title: Portfolio walk-through — 60 minutes
howWeHire.detail: Two projects, your choice. We care about the decisions and trade-offs, not the polish of the shots.

howWeHire.title: Paid design exercise — half a day, $400
howWeHire.detail: A real problem from our roadmap, on your schedule. Sketch-level fidelity is completely fine.

howWeHire.title: Offer within a week
howWeHire.detail: Two references, numbers in writing, a week to decide. We'll tell you the band before you start the exercise.

roles.title: Support Engineer
roles.oneLiner: Answer the hard tickets, reproduce the weird bugs, and be the reason a yard manager's Tuesday gets better.
whatYoudDo: Own the support inbox with two teammates — around forty conversations a day over email and phone, mostly from friendly non-technical yard staff.
Reproduce bugs properly and file reports engineers thank you for. You get a real staging environment and read access to the codebase.
Write and update the help docs whenever the same question shows up twice.
Spend Thursday afternoons with the product team, turning support patterns into roadmap arguments.
Work from the Portland office two or three days a week — spring launch season is all hands on deck, winters are genuinely quiet.
whatYouWont: No ticket quotas and no CSAT leaderboard. We measure whether problems actually got solved.
You won't be a human shield for engineering. Engineers take support rotations too and read tickets every week.

howWeHire.title: Intro call — 30 minutes
howWeHire.detail: With our support lead. Your story, our setup, and what a normal Tuesday actually looks like in the inbox.

howWeHire.title: Paid ticket exercise — 2 hours, $150
howWeHire.detail: Three real anonymized tickets. You write the replies on your own schedule; we talk through them together after.

howWeHire.title: Meet the team — 45 minutes
howWeHire.detail: Casual call with the two people you'd share the inbox with. Ask them anything — including what's annoying.

howWeHire.title: Offer within a week
howWeHire.detail: One reference, numbers in writing, a week to decide, and a proposed office-days schedule you can push back on.

roles.title: Onboarding Specialist
roles.oneLiner: Move new boatyards off paper binders and a 2004 Access database without losing a single slip record.
whatYoudDo: Run onboarding for four to six new yards a month: kickoff call, data import, training, and a check-in after their first billing run.
Clean up messy customer data — spreadsheets, ancient exports, sometimes literal paper — with our import tools and a careful eye.
Teach over video, and occasionally in person; some yards want you to walk their dock once before they trust the software.
Feed what you learn back to product. You'll know before anyone else which screens confuse new customers.
Work from the Portland office — imports run on a big second monitor next to the support team, and half the job is grabbing them for edge cases.
whatYouWont: No sales quotas. By the time a yard reaches you they've already bought; your job is making them glad they did.
You won't read from a script. Every yard's mess is different, and you're trusted to handle it your way.

howWeHire.title: Intro call — 30 minutes
howWeHire.detail: With our support lead. Your background, the job as it really is, and why this one is on-site.

howWeHire.title: Paid data exercise — 2 hours, $150
howWeHire.detail: One genuinely messy anonymized spreadsheet. Show us how you'd get it clean and what you'd ask the customer.

howWeHire.title: Office visit — half a day
howWeHire.detail: Sit with the team in Portland, watch a real onboarding call, and see the desk, the docks, and the coffee machine.

howWeHire.title: Offer within a week
howWeHire.detail: One reference, numbers in writing, and a week to decide. We'll cover travel costs for the visit either way.
